newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia building recovery widening - industry.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia building recovery widening - industry.

text.p: The Australian housing industry's recovery was broadening despite a fall in the number of building approvals in December, building industry groups said on Monday.

"The December building approvals show that the housing recovery, while still soft, is starting to broaden despite the one percent fall (seasonally adjusted) in the number of dwelling units approved," Master Builders Australia national director economics and housing Wilhelm Harnisch said in a statement.
Australian dwelling unit building approvals fell a seasonally-adjusted 1.0 percent in December to 10,836 from 10,942 in November, compared with 10,311 in December 1995.
Economists on average had expected building approvals to rise around 1.5 percent.
Harnisch said the best news from the figures was a 7.5 percent increase in the number of approvals for private sector houses.
"It is this segment of the market that needs to continue to increase in order for the housing recovery to become more robust and sustainable," Harnisch said.
However, he said a lack of consumer confidence was limiting the housing recovery and called for another 50 basis point cut in interest rates.
"Greatly improved affordability conditions are helping to rekindle buyer activity," he said
"The housing industry is looking for a restoration of home buyers' confidence and calls on the Reserve Bank to cut interest rates further," he said.
"A further reduction of 0.5 percent is justifiable given the low inflation outlook."
Housing Industry Association Ltd managing director Ron Silberberg said lower mortgage rates, stemming from the three interest cuts last year, were beginning to have an impact on the housing industry.
"Lower mortgage rates are starting to filter through to residential building activity," Silberberg said in a statement. -- Canberra Bureau 61-6 273-2730
